question: A man observes the top of a pole with an angle of elevation of 45°.He walks 15 m towards the pole, and the angle of elevation becomes 60°. What is the height of the pole?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the angle of elevation of an object of height 'h' changes from θ₁ to θ₂ upon moving distance 'd' towards it, the relation is:

d = h(cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)

⇒ 15 = h(cot 45° − cot 60°) = h(1 − 1/√3)

⇒ h = (15√3) / (√3 − 1)

⇒ Rationalising the denominator: h = 15(3 + √3) / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 15(3+√3)/2 m.**
